title: Make verifier check cited documents; flag self-covered map rows in code
summary: Closes two verification gaps seen in job 20261014-174815-7bf8. The verifier prompt now requires checking the change against any document the request cites, and falling short is a request-reading mismatch. Athena's own verdict code flags as major any candidate that moves a requirements-map row to Covered. Rows A9-1 and A10-1 go back to Partial with the reason. The audience is the user, who has to trust Athena's verdicts.

defaults_applied.how: The self-grading rule is enforced in verdict code, as the user asked. The document-comparison rule is explicitly marked prose-only.
New unit tests cover the code check, and the workspace test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Fixes the two process gaps (unchecked cited documents, self-graded rows) rather than only resetting the two rows.
A decision entry records the alternatives and tradeoff.
The decision entry cites job 20261014-174815-7bf8 and its verifier findings.
One focused change: two rules, one code check and two row fixes.
Docs, prompts and the changelog are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Core cannot call the CLI's strategy::parse_map, because athena-cli depends on core. So the check uses a small row parser in athena-core. A shared one could move into athena-data, but I assume the small duplicate is acceptable.
The check reads the map text at the base and at the candidate. run.rs already has git access to both, and the verifier's snapshot is one commit past the base. The producer picks the exact plumbing.
The finding is Athena-sourced, like the other Athena findings, so the verifier cannot omit it.
The user's reply fixes the scope to a major finding. It does not ask for a hard block beyond the normal fail verdict.
The document-comparison rule stays prose-only, because the repository cannot tell mechanically which documents a request cites. The change records that.
A9-1's missing piece is that the steward never calls a model. Nothing in this change builds that.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/verifier.md says that when the request cites a document (a file or section), the verifier reads it and compares the change with it, and that falling short is a request_reading_mismatch.

Athena's verdict code (crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, fed by crates/athena-core/src/run.rs) compares docs/design/requirements-map.md at the base with the candidate. For every row whose status changed to Covered from Partial or Not covered, or that was added already Covered, it adds an Athena-sourced major finding naming the row ID. So the final verdict cannot be pass. Rows that stay Covered, or move away from Covered, add no finding.

The producer prompt says a job may not mark its own requirement rows Covered. docs/enforcement.md or the decision entry records that this is enforced by code and that the document-comparison rule is prose-only.
In docs/design/requirements-map.md, A10-1 reads Partial: cost and yield tracking, reshaping and retiring are not built. A9-1 reads Partial: the steward never calls a model. Each cell says why.
The G5 counts in docs/design/strategy-view.md match the map, so A9-1 and A10-1 appear as Partial.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry with alternatives and the tradeoff, citing job 20261014-174815-7bf8 as the case. CHANGELOG.md notes the change. The roles-and-ladder doc stops describing A9-1 and A10-1 as covered, if it does.

Unit tests in verify.rs cover a row moved to Covered (major finding, verdict fail), a row left Covered (no finding), and a row moved away from Covered (no finding). Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-core verify
The token budgets still hold with the longer prompts. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
The whole workspace passes, including the strategy-view-against-map check. Run: cargo test --locked --workspace
The workspace is lint- and format-clean. Run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --check

out_of_scope: Making the steward call a model, which is the cause of the gap in A9-1.
Building cost and yield tracking, reshaping or retiring of roles (rest of A10-1).
Mechanically detecting which documents a request cites.
Changing the stored verification record schema beyond the new finding.
Re-reviewing or reverting the other changes from job 20261014-174815-7bf8.
departures: Higher cost than the reference: the change spans prompts, verdict code with a new input from run.rs, tests and several docs, and the token-budget test may need attention.
